parts.text: A skydiver jumps from an aeroplane. She falls freely with her parachute closed; then she opens her parachute. Fig. 1.1 shows the skydiver falling freely with her parachute closed. Fig. 1.2 shows the skydiver falling with the parachute open. Fig. 1.1 Fig. 1.2 Fig. 1.3 shows the speed–time graph for the skydiver’s vertical motion, from leaving the aeroplane to landing on the ground. Fig. 1.3

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Determine the maximum vertical speed of the skydiver. maximum speed = .................................................. m / s [1]

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Determine the distance the skydiver falls between time = 50 s and time = 80 s. distance = ...................................................... m [3]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The weight of the skydiver is 750 N. The weight of the skydiver acts downwards, as shown in Fig. 1.4. While the skydiver is falling, another force acts upwards. The upward force varies as the skydiver falls. ............................................. Fig. 1.4

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Fig. 1.4, write the name of the upward force on the dotted line above the upward force. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Suggest a value for the upward force on the skydiver at time = 10 s. ....................................................... N [1]
